We first write $50u^7$ as the product $25u^6\cdot 2u$ which contains a perfect square $(25u^6){:}$ 

$$
\eqalign{
	\sqrt{50u^7}&=\[3pt]
	\sqrt{25u^6\cdot 2u}&
	}
$$

Then, we separate the product into two separate radicals:

$$
\eqalign{
	\sqrt{25u^6\cdot 2u}&=\[3pt]
	\sqrt{\left(5u^3\right)^2\cdot 2u}&=\[3pt]
	\sqrt{\left(5u^3\right)^2}\cdot\sqrt{2u}&
	}
$$

Finally, we simplify the radical containing the perfect square:

$$
\eqalign{
	\sqrt{\left(5u^3\right)^2}\cdot\sqrt{2u}&=\[3pt]
	|5u^3|\cdot\sqrt{2u}&=\[3pt]
	|5|\cdot |u^3|\cdot\sqrt{2u}&=\[3pt]
	5|u|^3 \sqrt{2u}
	}
$$
